details: The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's Inflation Nowcasting tool forecasts the Consumer Price Index (CPI) to accelerate to 3.77% in October, with Core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) reaching 3.13%. This upward trend is primarily driven by rapidly rising fuel costs. While the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) is expected to hold interest rates steady at its meeting on October 27-28, market futures anticipate potential rate hikes, pushing the federal funds rate to approximately 4.5% by October 2027. This outlook signals a sustained period of restrictive monetary policy.
title: US Inflation Surges, Fed Eyes Further Rate Hikes

details: The World Bank's latest projections indicate a significant slowdown in global economic growth, with a forecast of 2.5% for 2026. This deceleration is largely attributed to the ongoing Middle East conflict, which is contributing to sharp energy price increases, renewed inflationary pressures, and expectations of tighter global monetary policies. The World Bank warns that risks to this outlook remain skewed to the downside.
title: World Bank Forecasts Global Growth Slowdown to 2.5% in 2026

details: Brent crude oil prices surged to an approximate range of $116-$117 per barrel on October 23, marking a five-month high. This increase is a direct consequence of escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and heightened concerns over potential disruptions to global oil supplies. The elevated oil prices are exacerbating persistent inflationary pressures worldwide.
title: Brent Crude Hits 5-Month High Amid Middle East Conflict

details: Global stock markets experienced notable declines, with major U.S. indices such as the S&P 500 falling by 1.2% and the Nasdaq 100 by 2.9% on October 23. This downturn was driven by a combination of investor concerns regarding the sustainability and profitability of extensive artificial intelligence (AI) technology investments, alongside the impact of surging oil prices. This confluence of factors has fostered a "risk-off" sentiment across financial markets.
title: Global Stocks Decline Amid AI Spending Concerns and Rising Oil Prices

details: U.S. consumer sentiment continued its decline for the third consecutive month in October, with the University of Michigan's Index of Consumer Sentiment weakening to 48. This drop reflects growing concerns among consumers about diminishing purchasing power and overall affordability, further pressured by persistently high interest rates. The average 30-year fixed mortgage rates remain elevated, recently reported at 7.32%.
sourceName: People's Daily Online (citing University of Michigan data)
title: US Consumer Sentiment Falls, High Mortgage Rates Persist
